title: Rest in the rule
hookLine: real rest, not only sleep: Antony showed a shocked hunter that a bow always bent will break
tomorrow: a man asked: tie my camel, or just trust God? what was the answer?

cards: A work text on a Saturday: quick question. Two minutes to answer, and somehow the whole day tilts toward the inbox. A hunter in the Egyptian desert once had firm ideas about how holy people should spend their time.
He came upon Abba Antony, the old hermit, sitting with the brothers, talking and enjoying their company, and he was shocked. Weren't monks supposed to be at prayer? Antony didn't argue.
He turned to the hunter's bow.

teach.b: Put an arrow to the string, he said, and shoot. The hunter did. Shoot another.

teach.h: A BOW ALWAYS BENT WILL BREAK.
teach.b: And the hunter said: if I keep bending my bow like this, it will break. So it is with the work of God, Antony said. Stretch the brothers beyond measure and they'll soon break.
Sometimes you have to come down and meet their needs. The hunter went away moved, and the brothers went home strengthened. Here's what the desert tradition made of it.

The monks had a name for what Antony showed: discretion, the sense of measure. John Cassian, who carried the desert teaching to the West, tells of a time the elders asked which virtue keeps a monk from falling. Fasting?
Keeping vigil? Giving everything away? Antony's answer was discretion, because it guards all the others.
Without it, even good practice becomes a bow drawn until it snaps.

teach.h: REST IS PART OF THE WORK.
teach.b: So in the desert, rest that isn't sleep, a meal together, talk, an easy hour with the brothers, wasn't a lapse from the work of God. It was part of it.

A bow doesn't rest by being left strung in a corner. It rests when the string comes off. Real rest in your rule is time when nothing is pulling at you, no quick questions, no inbox, so that when you draw again, it holds.

how: The desert monks prized discretion, the sense of measure, and kept time for rest and company alongside prayer. Some people on other paths keep a weekly day or evening free of work and screens.

games.q: what does “rest in the rule” mean?
o: a vacation you take once you've finished every task
a few extra hours of sleep added to the end of the week
time written in when you stop producing, beyond sleep

games.q: the hunter and the bow: tap the pairs.
p: if I bend my bow so, it will break
stretch the brothers too far, they break
the sense of measure that guards the rest

s: Antony told the hunter that monks should never stop praying
he showed him a bow: bent without rest, it breaks.
in the story, the brothers went home strengthened
the hunter left moved, and the brothers went home stronger.
rest in the desert tradition just meant sleeping
Antony was awake, enjoying the brothers' company: rest that isn't sleep.

games.q: a friend finally gets a free Saturday and fills it with chores and a side gig "to get ahead." what would Antony say?
o: take the string off: a bow always bent will break, and rest is part of the work.
nothing: chores are fine as long as you also sleep in.
rest only counts once the work is completely done.
games.why: Antony showed the hunter that a bow kept drawn breaks. Rest that isn't sleep belongs to the work, not after it.

practice: Put your phone out of reach and let your hands rest open on your lap, like a bow with the string taken off. For the whole sit, do nothing useful. If a to-do comes up, let it wait like a letter on the table, unopened.
Notice what your body does when nothing is asked of it.

wordCard.voice: Rest in the rule: time written in when nothing is pulling at you, not only sleep, the way Antony showed the hunter an unstrung bow.

orig.note: Greek: discernment, discretion. The desert monks' word for the sense of measure.

carryVoice: Your line: rest. Antony said a bow always bent will break, so take the string off. See you tomorrow, day 1651.

sources.ref: Sayings of the Desert Fathers (Apophthegmata Patrum), alphabetical collection, Antony 13 (a hunter is shocked to see Antony relaxing with the brothers; 'shoot again'; 'if I bend my bow so much I will break it'; so with the work of God; the brothers go home strengthened)
John Cassian, Conferences 2.2-4 (Abba Moses recalls the elders at Antony's asking which virtue keeps a monk from falling; Antony names discretion, which guards the others)
